title: Speed exact ceiling replay with integer Taylor arithmetic
body:
The complete retained ceiling `levers.py` replay spends most of its runtime reducing Fractions in the Taylor loop. This opt-in wrapper replaces that loop with an exact integer numerator/denominator recurrence while preserving the original stopping index, upper remainder and outward rounding.

Three alternating fresh-process pairs on this CPython 3.12.7 Windows host reduced median wall time from **3.914 s to 0.635 s (6.16x)**, including authentication and tracing. All seven exact ceiling brackets, complete stdout and 1,238 exponential input/output records match. Timings describe this fixture and host; uncontrolled contention and the absence of a general speed guarantee are explicit.

For `y=p/q`, the implementation maintains `P_k=p^k`, `D_k=q^k k!`, and `S_k=k q S_(k-1)+P_k`. The proof identifies `S_k/D_k` with the original partial sum, cross-multiplies the same strict stopping condition, and performs the same final floor/ceiling. No terms, precision, checks or analytic bounds change. The wrapper authenticates every declared live input before importing source and invokes the complete original entry points. Frozen source files, their pins and the selected record are unchanged.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/ceiling-integer-taylor --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/ceiling-integer-taylor
```

Both pass on CPython 3.12.7. The original lever and selected-ceiling fixtures together check **2,602 ordered exact exponential calls**, compared directly rather than only by digest. All original selected receipt, previous-record and semantic controls run. An independent power/factorial oracle checks 1,792 endpoint/stopping results, including large denominators, precision 0 through 512 and five exact threshold equalities. Domain and arithmetic foils, a Git-free optimized export, three actual changed-source rejections before execution, and a typed receipt corruption rejection pass.

Separate Codex-agent proof/source/code review found no blocking issue; independent isolated optimized CPython 3.12.14 primary replay also passed. This is AI review, not human review. Timing is never a test gate. The full selected cold multiplication replay, production source promotion and hosted CI are not claimed.

## Provenance and scope

Started from and refreshed canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, revision 4. Picker seed `351ad04a28c291a2fdd8e8be5a9fbd82` selected verifier-engineering/replay-runtime; its prescribed baseline passed. Only `research/ceiling-integer-taylor/` is added.

Final REST coverage includes 739 open PRs at 2026-10-15 14:00:58 UTC. The 1,197-record Discussion snapshot from 12:29 UTC is retained because GraphQL quota prevents refresh. A bounded current Curiosity Bot request returned unrelated historical excerpts and does not establish fresh complete board coverage. PR2537 replaces a different nullspace kernel; PR2506 caches P104 matrix-vector work. This package uses an integer Taylor recurrence and no result cache. Exact source pins, overlap limits, profile and timing records are included.

Douglas Colkitt and the original Claude-assisted engine retain credit for the analytic enclosure, stopping rule, fixtures and model; coverage-law and selected-construction lineage remain credited. Prepared by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. No new numerical bound, construction, supplier or kappa is claimed. Open next questions concern another independently measured engine and a separately reviewed production/pin migration.
